Subject: Moneta pool headroom audit & proposed remediations

Quick technical summary (observed between 08:20-09:50 PST):
- Dedicated pool for Moneta reached 96-100% GPU utilization for sustained 18 minutes.
- Scheduler queue length increased sharply; 95th/99th tail latency rose from ~120ms to 1.2s/3.9s.
- Error surface: primarily rate-limited 503s from the serving proxy due to request throttling after queue overflow.
- Root cause signal: sudden increase in concurrent short-context requests from a new client integration namespace + an internal Moneta scheduled data-sync that ramped concurrency.

Attachments: throughput-metrics.csv (minute-granularity), sample profiler logs.

Immediate remediation options (ranked):
1) Apply a temporary QoS limiter to the offending namespace and re-route lower-priority traffic to a smaller-quantized fallback model variant (expected immediate latency improvement, 5-10% throughput loss).
2) Increase reserved slots for Moneta by 20% for the next 24-72 hours (requires exec approval / billing adjustment) — removes throttling but will incur overage/commit change.
3) Short-term eviction of queued batch jobs and spin up an isolated auxiliary pool for non-critical workloads (operationally heavier, ~60-90m to provision).

I recommend option 1 now (fastest) + option 2 as a parallel exec-approved mitigation to prevent recurrence. I'm attaching minute-level metrics; the config snapshot is in pool-config.png.

I'll implement option 1 now unless I hear objections in the next 10 minutes.

-Vivek
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
